mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over three months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds +1%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase of more than 0.4 percentage points over two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >0.4pp for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in at least 70% of triggered instances (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% over three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings visibility and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual monetary tightening and inflationary pressure regime, which increases risk premia and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 5% over four consecutive months signals a robust residential construction cycle, which boosts materials and financial sector earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises by >5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 60% of triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month indicates a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to absorb new entrants, which dampens consumer confidence and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE also increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals reduced household buffer capacity, which increases reliance on credit and debt-servicing costs, ultimately producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically below zero at 90% confidence.
